feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader: clear positioning, relevant progression, and solid evidence of scope across web, content, analytics, and multimedia. It reads professionally, but impact would improve with more outcome-focused metrics, tighter consolidation of overlapping skills sections, and a few wording/style fixes.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear senior-level brand: the headline, summary, and career progression align well with digital strategy/communications leadership.  
- Good credibility: recognizable tools, platforms, and responsibilities are specific and believable, especially Drupal, GA4, BigQuery, and studio buildout.  
- Strong breadth with focus: combines strategy, operations, technical execution, and stakeholder coordination without feeling unfocused.

1. Top improvements  
- Add sharper results: several bullets describe responsibilities more than outcomes; include measurable impact on engagement, efficiency, conversions, campaign performance, or team/process improvements.  
- Reduce duplication: “Core Competencies,” “Topline Skills,” and “Technical + IT” overlap significantly; consolidate to save space and strengthen structure.  
- Fix style/consistency issues: “12 years experience” should be “12 years’ experience” or “more than 12 years of experience”; maintain consistent comma usage in lists (“workflows and systems” vs. “workflows, systems”); “A2/Learning” is stylistically awkward—use “French (A2, currently learning).” No major misspellings or obvious typos found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible summary that aligns with the CV, but it reads a bit generic and repeats themes already covered in Core Competencies and Topline Skills. It would be stronger with a clearer seniority signal and a few more distinctive, outcome-oriented phrases.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Change “more than 12 years experience” to “12+ years of experience” for cleaner style and grammar.
- Lead with your current level and niche: digital strategy, platform modernization, and communications operations for mission-driven/public-sector organizations.
- Replace broad phrases like “web, content, email, social media, and multimedia programs” with tighter wording such as “multi-channel digital communications.”
- Suggested rewrite: “Digital communications and strategy leader with 12+ years of experience leading multi-channel communications, web modernization, and content operations for mission-driven organizations. Brings deep expertise in cross-channel strategy, CMS and workflow design, and stakeholder coordination across complex teams. Strong background in advocacy and policy communications, translating technical issues into clear, accessible content and scalable digital systems.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-channel communications,” “platform modernization,” and “workflows and systems” are repeated in Core Competencies/Topline Skills.
- “Advocacy messaging” overlaps with multiple NACo role descriptions; keep it concise here.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header, Topline Skills, and Technical + IT sections. It would be more effective if tightened to emphasize higher-level strengths rather than repeating channel, workflow, and platform language.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use broader, executive-level phrasing and reduce overlap with detailed skills sections.
- Standardize style/pluralization: use parallel noun phrases rather than mixing functions and outputs.
- Consider rewrite: Digital strategy & transformation • Content operations & editorial governance • Web platform leadership • Cross-channel communications • Analytics, insights & performance reporting • Workflow design & systems improvement • Stakeholder & cross-functional leadership • Advocacy & policy communications • Multimedia production & live events
- If targeting more senior roles, swap “Web & CMS administration” for “Web platform leadership” to sound more strategic and current.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Multi-channel communication,” “stakeholder coordination,” and “policy & advocacy communication” repeat the header almost verbatim.
- “Web & CMS administration,” “data analytics & reporting,” and “multimedia & live event production” are already covered in more detail under Topline Skills/Technical + IT.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads broad and overlaps heavily with the header, skills, and recent projects. Tighten it around 3–4 high-impact outcomes and name the organization if possible.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + client type: “Embedded strategic communications consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform improvements across web, campaigns, analytics, and content operations.”
- Replace generic verbs with outcome-oriented phrasing: “Built organization-wide workflows, analytics, and governance systems to improve coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Combine Drupal/CMS bullets: “Designed and implemented Drupal campaign experiences, including modular microsites, storytelling components, downloadable toolkits, and front-end/CMS enhancements for public-facing properties.”
- Keep the AI work, but sharpen it: “Led an AI-enabled search initiative spanning retrieval design, structured content workflows, and user discovery experience.” Add metrics if available (sites launched, users served, time saved, engagement lift).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Governance, analytics, workflows” repeats NACo Director role and header language; keep only if tied to new outcomes.
- Detailed microsite/AI examples also appear in Recent Projects; avoid repeating the same wording.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. It should be tightened to foreground the biggest outcomes and avoid repeating channel-management themes already covered in earlier NACo roles.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed enterprise digital communications, platform modernization, analytics, governance, and budget for NACo’s web, email, social, and video ecosystem.”
- Combine and prioritize the strongest achievements: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal site serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make outcomes more explicit where possible: add % improvements in publishing efficiency, reporting speed, engagement, production cost savings, or reduced agency/vendor reliance from the in-house studio.
- Tighten weaker bullets by emphasizing business value: e.g., “Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house studio, increasing advocacy/event production capacity,” and “Implemented GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery reporting to improve leadership visibility and decision-making.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Video-programming language also echoes prior NACo roles; stress the studio build and scaled operational impact instead.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more clearly about executional leadership, editorial operations, and channel growth before the broader strategic scope of the 2022–2024 position.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize operational ownership: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, improving editorial coordination and advocacy content delivery.”
- Tighten bullets and foreground scale/outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more impact-focused: “Launched and produced a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine the last two bullets into one sharper line: “Built stronger cross-team editorial planning and more consistent digital publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Helped improve” is too soft and repeats the governance/workflow theme already covered more strongly in the Director role.
- “Produced and expanded” overlaps with the earlier Digital Media Manager entry; here, stress scaling/operationalizing rather than initial creation.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong themes, but this item overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. It should be tightened to emphasize distinctive leadership strengths rather than repeat broad digital/communications language.

Suggested edit:
- Replace generic phrases with sharper, less redundant wording:
- Enterprise web and content strategy
- Editorial governance and publishing operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy communications
- Audience-centered content planning
- Consider swapping one line for a more current differentiator from recent work, e.g. “AI-enabled content discovery strategy” or “Digital governance for complex publishing teams.”
- Keep wording noun-based and parallel; avoid mixing “messaging” with broader operational capabilities.
- If space allows, prioritize enterprise governance and platform strategy over general content planning, since those are stronger and more senior signals.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Multi-channel communications leadership” repeat the header/Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with “Advocacy and public-sector communications”; use one version only.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong skill mix, but this item is too long and overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies” and “Technical + IT.” Make it sharper by emphasizing the most relevant, recent platform strengths and grouping lower-priority tools.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from a raw list to tighter capability clusters: “Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint & Power Pages • CMS modernization & front-end implementation • API integrations & workflow automation • Airtable systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Prioritize recent, differentiating strengths first: lead with Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, and integrations; these are best supported by recent roles/projects.
- Remove “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” from this topline section or shorten to “front-end implementation”; detailed coding tools already appear in Technical + IT.
- If space allows, make one item outcome-oriented: “CMS modernization for high-volume public-sector sites” to connect directly to the 10,000+ page Drupal migration.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Significant overlap with “Core Competencies” on CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, and workflow automation.
- Significant overlap with “Technical + IT” on platforms and coding languages.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:

- Looker Studio
- Power BI

items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a generic inventory and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” analytics section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value capabilities and decision-making impact rather than repeat software names.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool list to capability-led phrasing, e.g. “Analytics strategy, KPI design & executive reporting.”
- Trim to 5–6 items max; keep only the most differentiating tools: “GA4, BigQuery, Power BI/Looker Studio, Microsoft Clarity.”
- Replace “SEO and performance analysis” with broader, stronger language like “search and content performance optimization.”
- Suggested rewrite: “Analytics strategy & KPI design • Executive and leadership reporting • GA4, BigQuery, Power BI & Looker Studio • User behavior analysis with Microsoft Clarity • Search, content and conversion performance optimization”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current tool list duplicates “Technical + IT > Data, Analytics & Optimization”; keep detailed platforms there and make this section more strategic.
- “Leadership reporting” also overlaps with “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant platform list, but it’s too bare and duplicates the stronger “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” section. This item should either be tightened to emphasize depth/relevance or removed to avoid repeating the same keywords.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by strongest/recent platform: “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages” is fine, but consider signaling proficiency: “Drupal (primary) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages.”
- If space allows, add a light qualifier tied to recent work: “Enterprise CMS: Drupal (10,000+ page migration), WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages, GitHub Pages.”
- Keep naming consistent with other technical sections; avoid mixing “platforms” and “execution” language unless this section is meant to be platform-only.
- If this section stays, make it clearly distinct from coding/automation by labeling it “CMS & Web Platforms.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This substantially overlaps with Topline Skills [2]; consider keeping the fuller Topline version and deleting this item.
- Drupal is already strongly evidenced in recent roles, so repeating it without context adds little value.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This section should feel more implementation-focused and current, emphasizing tools that support recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from broad coding languages to applied delivery: “Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API and tag management integrations • Edge scripting with Cloudflare Workers • Deployment automation with GitHub Actions”
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) for cleaner, more senior phrasing.
- If accurate, add scope/outcome context in adjacent experience bullets rather than here, e.g., GTM used for analytics/event tracking or Workers/Actions used for deployment/workflow automation.
- Order by relevance to recent work: JavaScript / API integrations / GTM / Cloudflare Workers / GitHub Actions / HTML / CSS / jQuery.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Strong overlap with Topline Skills [2] (“HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery • API integrations”). Keep this item more tool-specific and implementation-oriented.
- “Workflow automation” is already covered elsewhere; avoid implying GitHub Actions does the same thing unless you specify deployment/CI.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow automation capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe to emphasize systems-building, not just apps: “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Systems: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp; Slack and Microsoft Teams.”
- Group by function to improve scanability and reduce clutter: automation tools first, then project/work management, then collaboration platforms.
- If true, add a qualifier tied to recent work impact, e.g. “used to streamline editorial planning, approvals, reporting, and cross-team communications.”
- Consider dropping one lower-value/older platform if space is tight (e.g. Basecamp or Trello) to keep the list sharper and more current.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same phrasing elsewhere.
- Slack/Teams are common collaboration tools; keep them only if they support a broader systems/operations narrative.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Clear and relevant, but it reads as a generic tool list. Since email leadership already appears strongly in recent NACo roles, this item should emphasize platform breadth and avoid overstating email strategy here.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as: “Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp”
- If space allows, add light functional context: “Email marketing, newsletter operations and audience engagement platforms: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp”
- Keep product names consistent and current; “Customer Insights / Journeys” is good, but use one standard format throughout the CV if referenced elsewhere.
- Only include platforms you’ve used meaningfully in recent roles; if one was limited or older, consider dropping it to keep this section sharper.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Email/newsletter leadership is already covered in recent work experience, so don’t add claims like “managed large-scale email campaigns” here.
- “Audience engagement” overlaps with core competencies; keep this item tool-focused rather than descriptive.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the 2018–2024 NACo roles. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with concrete outputs if you can add metrics.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to emphasize early-team building and production execution: “Promoted across two digital roles while helping establish NACo’s first in-house digital team and standardize workflows across web, email, social and multimedia.”
- Add 1–2 specific outputs with scale: website refresh scope, number/frequency of livestreams or weekly videos, audience reach, or engagement gains.
- Tighten the management point: replace “providing day-to-day guidance” with “mentored a digital media associate on production and publishing workflows.”
- Consider a concise version: “Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestream and weekly video content, and helped formalize cross-channel publishing processes.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; frame this as launching or early production support, not expansion.
- Avoid repeating workflow/governance language already used more strongly in the later NACo entries.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows initiative, especially the first podcast launch. It should be tightened to emphasize ownership and outcomes, while avoiding overlap with later NACo digital/media roles.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the standout achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities; launched NACo’s first podcast, leading planning, scripting, and production.”
- Add one concise supporting clause on content work: “Produced digital and multimedia content to support program communications and policy storytelling.”
- If possible, quantify impact: number of episodes launched, audience/downloads, internal stakeholders supported, or projects delivered.
- Keep this entry shorter than later NACo roles since those better represent your senior digital leadership.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia materials” overlaps with later Digital Media Manager / Producer and Associate Communications Director entries; keep this version higher-level.
- Avoid repeating video/livestream language here unless this role clearly owned a distinct first or measurable result.
